# the contributor audits of three distinct mechanisms

## Global baseline curvature and the smallest-fiber mode

The root read every section of
`candidate 9040ddab36f28107`, ran its
verifier (PASS), and independently derived its full completion of squares
before reading the final file. The source identity retains the original
global cap baseline. Its pure parameter second derivative is therefore
G'', not zero merely because a radial regularization preserved the
original tuple's budgets. The stated regularity assumption is C2 and is
not inferred from properness alone.

The absolute right inverse, positive multipliers, first-order criterion,
and strict second-order if-and-only-if statement have the correct units.
The coarea correction retains both the acceleration and the derivative
of weighted section second moments. The same-meeting homothetic chart
has G_i=V sum(r_z h-tau_i)^d, giving exactly the displayed moment sums S
and N2. Criticality imposes zero trace and row sums mS v.

Independently, for fixed diagonal b and row sums r, minimizing the squared
off-diagonal norm under zero column sums gives

    A_ij=[d r_i+r_j-m(b_i+b_j)]/[m(d-1)],
    ||A||^2=[d||r||^2-2m r.b+2m||b||^2]/[m(d-1)].

Orthogonal zero-row/column residuals then give the complete negative
square, not merely a lower bound. Maximizing in b gives
b=[d^2(S-1)+1]v and the exact residual coefficient
m(d-1)[d(S-1)^2+1-N2]/d. This agrees with (18)-(20).
For a smallest-radius choice, the displayed power-sum comparison makes
the coefficient strictly positive whenever another fiber exists.
For the two-fiber heavy-choice example its strict negativity gives a
negative-definite Hessian on all critical variables in the specified
chart. Surjectivity and positive multipliers justify the local cap-
inequality conclusion; it does not address a larger normal-motion chart.

The preliminary radial barrier is exactly flat only at the original cap
tuple, which is sufficient here. Analytic proper simplex formulas give
the required convergence of the full baseline and its derivatives. The
remaining construction chooses its physical motion after opening actual
compatibility, preserving every selected cap inequality and increasing
mass. All other original groups are outside the theorem's scope.

The equal-fraction addendum also passes. A strict slab argument puts the
ordinary centroid at the common meeting point. The covering caps bound
the ordinary maximum depth above by Gamma, so the previously audited
ordinary equality rigidity gives a simplex. The archived single-cap
equality theorem identifies each oriented opposite-facet normal. The
one-dimensional normal dependence then forces a common positive scaling,
which proves aligned homothety. No extra multiple-cap rigidity assumption
is needed.

## Finite radial nonincrease cone

The root fully read `candidate f0b371d38574bbcc`
and ran the correctly named `supporting computation verify_finite_radial_cap_budget_cone.py`:

fans and extreme excluded-target representations gives a finite exact
compatibility test. Positive derivatives on all active ray rows, and the
old positive inactive rows, give a uniform all-direction margin. The
volume-coordinate path has exactly affine total and through-section cap
costs. The Farkas signs in A^T alpha=C^T beta+eta w are correct.

For a proper oblique trace, differentiating r^d F(tau/r) gives the extra
positive term tau S/d in volume coordinates. Weak derivatives alone do
not imply finite nonincrease; the note correctly requires strict signs
there or retains exact through-section/full-empty formulas. Source cover
preservation is separately justified only for full-fiber covers or a
uniform strict neighborhood. The complementary-cap dual calibration and
the endpoint-only positive calibration both have the stated scope.
This cone is a proved finite criterion, not universal feasibility.

## Base scale/phase deformation and positive-width sample events

The root fully read `candidate a754d14c81eb6c11`
and ran its verifier: PASS. Reflection plus convexity of depth superlevel
sets proves the midpoint optimal in each fiber, so the exact formulas
optimize over all actual points. The clipped linear cap mass retains all
tilts; finite steep caps dominate the vertical candidates. Empty-trace
events and outer constant pieces contain a minimizer even with simultaneous
events or flat pieces. The event substitution gives the finite formula
and its piecewise affine dependence on the affine width parameter.

The three-fiber centered submeasure gives the exact middle lower bound,
and a single steep cap attains it. The resulting ratio has the unique
minimum at (1,3,5). The fixed trapezoid really has a two-parameter open
chamber, with ridge t=(s-1)/2 and the stated endpoints. At the lower
endpoint the disappearing positive-width fiber remains included because
the body is closed; at the upper endpoint the entering positive-width
fiber is already included. The exact boundary profiles give respectively
the one-sided jump to 3/8 and the entrance value 13/32.

The root separately computed the four-fiber midpoint depths and all four
upper-cover slopes, confirming (1/2,5/2,13/2,7/2). Within the three-fiber
chamber the sublevel set at 5/18 is exactly the ridge. Its two exits thus
prove that a continuous nonincreasing path cannot proceed through a count
change, although it can reach the support-loss contact. This is a fixed-
deformation obstruction; replacing the body repeatedly by its sampled
hull would change the deformation, as explicitly acknowledged. Zero-width
events have a different, continuous limit. None of these examples is
below the OC target.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
